items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: And we had a fella, uh, Leonard Phillips. He was playing trumpet. And King Oliver was playing trumpet... I stayed with Walter Johnson until 1934... By that time King Oliver sent for me. And I was back again with King Oliver.

ctx.x: Did he limp a little bit? Yeah, that's right. Piano player. I didn't know he was down here. I didn't know he came back.

Yeah, he came down here and he pulled those boys and so they got me out the band for a while. And so they fought so much over the band, I just quit and I left the band to go. I quit the band. After I quit the band, the band just went down. So I joined the band with Walter Johnson. Had a fella they called Walter Johnson. So I joined with Walter Johnson's band and we did pretty good work around there. And we got the job at the American Legion that Gabriel had the job there for about ten years and we got the job…
Where did most of those people come from? Any certain part of the country? They weren't from New Orleans, I guess. No, no.

items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: The personnel listed then was Herman "Red" Elkins, you and King Oliver on trumpets; Pete Jones on trombone; Buddy Harold and Paul Barnes on altos.

ctx.x: He wanted to take over the band.

Yeah. So Bronson left, I think, around about... I remember the last dance we played under Bronson was Christmas -- Christmas of '31. The Christmas Holidays of '31. Then a guy named Tiny Taylor that sang with the band, he took it out for a while. He was going to sing with King's band anyway. So they got some dates, and Frederick Brothers... This was a big booking agency that was in Wichita. Frederick Brothers was booking King's other band, and he heard this band... They was telling him, "King, take this band. We…
They were in King Oliver's band before you joined.
